top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) is the only writer on the slate, and I rank him first on literary grounds. As publicly described, Blinding (the first volume of the Orbitor sequence) and Solenoid show an unmistakable voice, dense patterned prose, and a large formal architecture that treats memory, the body and dream as one imaginative system. The major structures are published, so the whole authorship can be assessed now. The citation is single-writer and single-language, centred on the prose with poetry named only as foundation. This matches the round-2 wording. Open questions remain: how much sentence-level density in Romanian survives translation, whether the later volumes advance the project or only enlarge it, and how much weight the poetry can bear. I have not read the corpus independently or verified sources. I do not count the unanimity of the opening rankings as merit. I see no literary reason in the evidence to prefer no award (P000), so it ranks last. The remaining doubts concern evidence and verification, not a finding that the work falls short.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile; documented ties are collegial only (2019 renewal round with Ellen Mattson, service with Olsson, Mattson, Sem-Sandberg, Palm). My 2021 public statement on women's authorships is attributed context and not evidence of merit. I have not used gender, nationality or language in assessing the candidate. Self-reported from the supplied profile and not independently verified.
